name: Peak near Cabeus B
blurb: Elevated peak near Cabeus B with good sunlight and Earth view, beside Cabeus cold traps where LCROSS detected water.

name: Haworth
blurb: Region by Haworth crater, a large permanently shadowed cold trap likely to hold water ice.

name: Malapert Massif
blurb: Tall massif with continuous Earth line of sight and long sunlit periods near polar cold traps.

name: Mons Mouton Plateau
blurb: Broad plateau next to Mons Mouton; flat sunlit terrain near shadowed craters that may trap volatiles.

name: Mons Mouton
blurb: Lunar south pole mountain chosen for VIPER; sunlit slopes beside cold traps that may hold water ice.

name: Nobile Rim 1
blurb: Rim of Nobile crater, whose shadowed floor is a cold trap and potential water ice reservoir.

name: Nobile Rim 2
blurb: Second Nobile rim region with access to ancient crust and nearby permanently shadowed regions.

name: de Gerlache Rim 2
blurb: Rim of de Gerlache crater near the pole, with high illumination and shadowed cold traps close by.

name: Slater Plain
blurb: Plains north of Slater crater, added in 2024; relatively smooth terrain near south polar cold traps.

name: Shackleton rim / Connecting Ridge
blurb: Ridge linking Shackleton and de Gerlache; near-continuous sunlight next to Shackleton's permanently shadowed floor.

name: Shiv Shakti point (Chandrayaan-3)
blurb: First soft landing at high southern latitude; Pragyan measured sulphur and regolith temperature in situ.

name: Jezero crater (Perseverance)
blurb: Ancient lake delta where Perseverance caches samples for Mars Sample Return and seeks biosignatures.

name: Gale crater (Curiosity)
blurb: Layered Mount Sharp sediments record a habitable lake environment and Mars' shift to a drier climate.

name: Oxia Planum (Rosalind Franklin)
blurb: Clay-rich Noachian plains where the rover will drill 2 m deep to search for preserved organic molecules.

name: Utopia Planitia (Viking 2)
blurb: Viking 2 saw winter frost here; Utopia's mid-latitude plains hold extensive buried ground ice.

name: Southern Utopia Planitia (Zhurong)
blurb: Zhurong's radar found buried layered deposits, hinting at past water at the edge of a possible northern ocean.

name: Elysium Planitia (InSight)
blurb: Flat equatorial plain where InSight's seismometer mapped Mars' crust, mantle and core.

name: Meridiani Planum (Opportunity)
blurb: Hematite plains where Opportunity found sulfate sandstones from ancient acidic groundwater.

name: Gusev crater (Spirit)
blurb: Spirit found silica deposits at Home Plate, evidence of ancient hot springs or fumaroles.

name: Green Valley (Phoenix)
blurb: Phoenix scraped into shallow water ice and detected perchlorate in polar soil.

name: Arcadia Planitia (SpaceX Starship candidate)
blurb: Mid-latitude plains with shallow ground ice mapped by SWIM; a leading candidate for crewed landings.

name: Deuteronilus Mensae
blurb: Lobate debris aprons that SHARAD shows are buried glacial ice, a water resource for human explorers.

name: Chryse Planitia (Viking 1)
blurb: First successful Mars landing; outflow channel plains where Viking ran the first life-detection experiments.

name: Ares Vallis (Mars Pathfinder)
blurb: Flood-deposited boulders at the mouth of Ares Vallis, explored by Sojourner, the first Mars rover.

name: Melas Chasma (Valles Marineris)
blurb: Central Valles Marineris trough with hydrated sulfates and layered deposits; proposed human exploration zone.

name: Arsia Mons cave skylights
mission: Mars Odyssey THEMIS / MRO HiRISE cave candidates
blurb: Seven candidate lava-tube skylights on the north flank of Arsia Mons: radiation-shielded shelter for crews and a place where ice and biosignatures could survive.
